title: Applicability of Large Language Models and Generative Models for Legal Case Judgement Summarization

model.params_source: assumed for temperature (paper silent); max_tokens per Sec. 4.4 is set per item to the target length (YY words ~ 1.33*YY tokens), 2048 is the cap; snapshot by the date rule

task.subset_rule: paper-defined split: UK-Abs test set (100 judgments)
task.approximation: Whole judgment in one prompt (128K context, Sec. 4.2) with YY = reference summary word count (Sec. 4.4 rule K*|Exp|/|Doc| with a single chunk); ROUGE implementation settings not stated. ROUGE-L is the runner's LCS-based F1 over lowercased whitespace tokens (rouge-score's rougeL tokenizer differs slightly).

items.source: https://zenodo.org/record/7152317 (dataset.zip 97.8 MB; folder UK-Abs/test-data with judgement/ and summary/full/; linked from github.com/Law-AI/summarization)

prompt.source_location: Sec. 4.2.3 (i) gpt4-summ; Sec. 4.4 'Deciding the target summary length'

placeholders_prose.YY: word count of the reference summary (Sec. 4.4 target-length rule)

metric.name: rouge_l
metric.definition: ROUGE-L F1 between the generated and the gold summary, averaged over the 100 test judgments (use rouge-score defaults without stemming)

notes: Inputs average 14,476 words (~20k tokens) so each call costs ~$0.23.
